question: Should this hardening land as a breaking pre-release cutover, or should it preserve current audit logs and identity CLI compatibility before merge?
rationale: The branch intentionally removes compatibility paths while changing stored audit data and CLI surface; only maintainers can decide whether that is acceptable for Turnwire's release state.

options.title: Preserve compatibility before merge
options.body: Add an audit migration/import path, keep `turnwire identity [--json]` as an alias, and prove both fresh-install and upgrade behavior before landing.

options.title: Approve a breaking cutover
options.body: Maintainers can explicitly accept the audit and CLI break with a clear operator recovery plan and release note.

options.title: Split the hardening
options.body: Pause this broad branch and land audit encryption, budgets, identity lifecycle, and release automation as smaller proof-backed PRs.

recommendation.title: Preserve compatibility before merge
recommendation.body: Add an audit migration/import path, keep `turnwire identity [--json]` as an alias, and prove both fresh-install and upgrade behavior before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: The same history owns the central audit, CLI, and secure channel behavior affected by the compatibility choice.
